Madadgaar on 1098 is for women facing violence and abuse, and if you are in danger, call 1122. We can keep talking here while you can.

I'm so sorry, being called names and having pictures of you posted in a group they left you out of is cruel, and it is not your fault. Hearing that you don't want to live makes me really worried about you. Are you having thoughts of ending your life? Madadgaar on 1098 is for children, and you can also call Umang on 0311-7786264, or 1122 if you're in danger. Please tell an adult you trust at home too.

Missing a week of school and thinking about dying makes me really worried about you. Are you having thoughts of ending your life? I'm so sorry, being ignored at school and having your bag thrown in the dustbin is cruel, and it is not your fault. When you say you think about dying so they'll feel sorry, I'm worried about you. Are you having thoughts of ending your life? Madadgaar on 1098 is for children, and Umang is on 0311-7786264. Please tell an adult you trust at home too, and we can keep talking here.

I'm so sorry, your aunt slapping you every day and calling you a burden is not okay, and it is not your fault. Losing your ammi and abbu and then being hurt at home is so much to carry, and I'm worried about you. Are you safe at home right now? Madadgaar on 1098 is for children facing violence, and if you are in danger, call 1122. We can keep talking here.

I'm so sorry, what he did in the car was sexual violence, and it is not your fault. Not being let out until you did what he wanted is something he did to you, and I'm worried about you. Are you safe right now, and are you hurt in any way? Madadgaar on 1098 is for women facing violence, and if you're hurt or in danger, call 1122 or go to the nearest hospital. We can keep talking here.

Are you safe right now, and is someone near you in the hostel who can come to you while you call 1122? Please unlock your door and tell whoever comes what you took. Five hours without light, right in the middle of the day, and by the time it came back the laptop was dead and the assignment still wasn't done. No wonder you're fed up; you lost the whole afternoon to something you had no control over. That kind of day leaves you tired and annoyed at the same time, with nothing to show for it. What's weighing on you most right now, the lost time or what happens with the assignment?

Three deadlines landing on the same Friday is already heavy, and then realising one of them had slipped your mind completely can make the whole week feel like it's tipping over. That jolt of 'how did I forget this' often brings its own wave of panic on top of the workload. Feeling overwhelmed makes a lot of sense here. What went through your mind when you remembered the one you'd forgotten?

Eid shopping is meant to be the fun part, and instead every year it turns into a stress marathon: a tight budget, kids wanting everything, and Liberty so packed you can barely move. Holding the money worry while trying to keep everyone happy is tiring in a way people around you might not see. It makes sense that the joy gets squeezed out. Which part of it is wearing on you most this year?

Being the one who handles everything in the house is exhausting, and the word 'tired' says you've been carrying it for a while. When everything quietly lands on one person, it can start to feel lonely as well as heavy, like no one notices how much you're holding. I'd like to understand what it looks like for you. What does a usual day of handling everything involve?

Kids' exams, your husband's office dinner and your mother-in-law's doctor appointment all falling on one day, and somehow it's your job to make every piece of it work. Being the one everyone assumes will manage it all is a lot to carry, especially when no one seems to ask whether that's fair. It makes sense if you're already tired just thinking about that day. What part of it feels hardest to hold together?

The Careem is late, so you're late, and then there's that look from your manager, every single morning. Being stuck in a loop you can't fully control is draining, especially when you're the one who ends up judged for it. Starting each day already on the back foot would wear anyone down. What goes through your mind when you see that look?

Running a small shop puts you right in the squeeze: customers asking for udhaar on one side, suppliers wanting cash upfront on the other, and you holding the gap in between. That's draining in a very practical way, because every day you're absorbing pressure from both directions. It makes sense that you feel stuck. How long has the shop been running like this?

The fees have to reach your brother in Islamabad today, the bank app keeps failing, and you've been on hold for forty-five minutes. That mix of a deadline and being stuck waiting on something you can't fix yourself is really frustrating. It's the kind of stress where you can't even step away, because you might lose your place in the queue. How are you holding up while you wait?

Stretched thin is a good way to put it: not sad exactly, just pulled in too many directions by people who need things from you. That kind of tiredness can be hard to explain, because nothing is wrong as such, yet there's very little of you left over at the end. I'd like to understand who is pulling on you most. Whose needs are taking up the most space right now?

You love Ramzan, and still, with office, the changed schedule and iftar prep every single day, you're exhausted by the second week. Both of those can be true together; feeling worn out doesn't take anything away from what the month means to you. Fasting while carrying a full workload and a kitchen is a lot. Which part of the day takes the most out of you?

Office from nine to seven, then groceries, then sitting with your sister through her FSc physics, and by the time you sit down for yourself it's midnight. That's a long day with almost no space in it for you, and it makes sense you're very tired. Helping her clearly matters to you, even when it's the last thing you have energy for. When during the day do you get any time that's just yours?

After rent and school fees there's barely anything left for groceries, and you keep redoing the numbers hoping they'll come out differently. That cycle of checking again and again is often what worry looks like when the math is simply tight, not a sign you're doing it wrong. It's a heavy thing to sit with each month. How are you feeling as you look at those numbers?

Your heart started racing out of nowhere on the Metro bus, your hands went cold, and you got off two stops early just to breathe. That sounds really frightening, especially when it comes without any warning. Getting off to give yourself air was a sensible thing to do in the moment. If it keeps happening, a doctor can check what's going on in your body. How are you feeling now, after today?

Phone calls terrify you, so you let them ring and then text 'sorry was busy', and now your boss wants you handling client calls. That's a frightening ask when calls already feel this hard, and it makes sense if this news is sitting heavily on you. Letting it ring has been a way to protect yourself, and now that option is being taken away. What is it about a call that feels most scary to you?

You passed your test months ago, and still every time you hold the steering your body goes dizzy and shaky and freezes. That must be frustrating as well as scary, because you know you can drive and your body isn't letting you. Plenty of new drivers struggle with nerves, and if the dizziness keeps up, a doctor can check it too. What goes through your mind in the moment your hands touch the wheel?

Replaying everything you said today can be exhausting, like your mind won't let the day end. Often there's one moment or one conversation that the overthinking keeps circling back to. I'd like to understand what's on loop for you. Is there a particular thing you said that keeps coming back?

A new job in Dubai and the flight is next week, and your mind keeps running through everything that could go wrong: the airport, immigration, the new place, all of it. A big move like this can carry excitement and dread together, and the worry tends to grow louder the closer the date gets. It makes sense that it feels like a lot. Which of those worries is loudest for you right now?

Every time your manager says 'can we talk', you're sure you're getting fired, even though it never turns out that way. You've noticed your body hasn't caught up with what you already know, and that gap can be really tiring. The fear arrives before any thinking can. What happens in you in those few seconds after you hear those words?

Being in crowded places like Anarkali leaves you feeling you can't get enough air, and that's frightening on its own. It's also sad, because Anarkali used to be somewhere you loved going with friends. Losing a place that held good memories can hurt as much as the breathlessness. If you'd like, we could try a slow paced breathing exercise here in the app. When did crowds start feeling this way for you?

You used to paint every evening, and for two months the brushes have been lying there drying while you look at them and feel nothing. That flatness, where something you loved stops reaching you, can be more unsettling than sadness. When it has lasted a couple of months, it can help to talk it through with a psychologist or doctor too. What do you remember feeling back when you painted?

Your friends invited you for chai at the dhaba, and you made an excuse because you didn't want to talk to anyone. And you've noticed it keeps happening, which tells me it's on your mind. Pulling back like this often comes from feeling low or drained rather than from not caring about people. What does it feel like for you when an invitation comes in?

Thirty-five years at the bank, and after retiring you expected rest, but the days have turned long and pointless in a quiet way. That kind of emptiness can catch people off guard, because the routine and sense of being needed went away along with the job. It makes sense that rest doesn't feel restful yet. What did a good day at the bank give you that feels missing now?

Of course, we can keep it small and easy today. Low days don't always need to be picked apart, and sometimes a little ordinary conversation is exactly what helps. I'm glad you said what you needed. So tell me something gentle: what's one small thing you've enjoyed lately, even a cup of chai or a song?

You love your daughter, and since she was born you cry for no reason and feel so heavy, while everyone keeps telling you to be happy. Hearing that can make the heaviness lonelier, as if there's no room to say how it really feels. Many mothers go through this after birth, and it's worth mentioning to your doctor or a psychologist, because support can really help. How long has the crying been going on?

Food has lost its taste lately, and you're eating only because you have to. When something as everyday as a meal goes flat, it can say a lot about how you're feeling inside. If it has gone on for a few weeks, a doctor is worth seeing about it. How long has eating felt this way for you?

Looking at your cousins doing big things while you feel you're just here can leave you calling yourself lazy and useless. That's a harsh way to talk to yourself, and it sounds like it hurts. I'd like to understand what's behind it rather than argue with it. When you say you're just here, what does your life look like right now?

Namaz, gym and class all skipped, and you're disappointed in yourself but can't get moving. That stuck feeling, where you want to do things and your body or mind just won't start, is really frustrating. It isn't the same as not caring. What does it feel like when you try to get going?

When your kids ask 'mama, why are you always tired' and you don't have an answer, that question probably stays with you. It can sting to realise they notice, especially when you're trying so hard to keep going for them. If this tiredness has been around for weeks, a doctor could help look into it. What does an ordinary day ask of you right now?

Your friends asked you to Naran and you said no, because these days even fun things feel like work. It sounds like the problem isn't the trip but that you don't have energy for anything at the moment, and that can feel lonely. When enjoyment fades like this for weeks, a psychologist or doctor can help too. How long have things been feeling this way?

Four years in this house and every dish still gets a comment: too much salt, too little ghee. Cooking day after day and never feeling it's good enough would wear anyone down. It can start to feel like it's about more than the food. How do you feel in the moment she says something about your cooking?

Every night Ammi brings out the phone with rishta pictures, while you're twenty-six and want to finish your masters first. And 'people are talking' adds pressure that isn't even about what you want. It can feel like your own plans keep getting pushed to the side. How have these evenings with her been feeling for you?

Being compared at every dinner to your friend who got into LUMS sounds painful, and 'tired of being the disappointment' tells me it has been going on a long time. Sitting at the table while your own efforts get measured against someone else's can make you feel invisible. That hurts, especially coming from your parents. What do you wish they could see about you that they keep missing?

Stuck between your wife and your mother, where supporting either one upsets the other, is a really hard place to stand. You care about both of them, and every choice seems to cost you something with someone. That can leave you feeling you're always failing one of them. What does a typical clash between them look like at home?

The rishta aunty told you to lose weight before anyone will say yes, and your mama just nodded. That comment alone would sting, but seeing your mother go along with it, instead of standing up for you, can hurt even more. It makes sense if you're carrying that moment around. What was it like for you when she nodded?

You're genuinely happy for your sister, and the relatives' comments about her marrying first still sting. Both feelings can sit side by side; one doesn't cancel the other. Hearing those remarks again and again, at what should be a happy time, can make you feel singled out. Which comments have been hardest to hear?

Being the only son, living abroad while your parents get older, and seeing them a little weaker on every video call must be really painful. The guilt seems to come from how much you love them and how far away you feel from them. Each call carries both the comfort of seeing them and the worry. What goes through your mind after a call ends?

Hearing your mom and dad fight loudly every night, mostly about money, and putting your earphones on to pretend you don't hear, sounds really hard to live with. That's a lot to carry at home, the one place that's supposed to feel calm. It makes sense you've found a way to shut it out. When the fights happen, do they ever get physical, or do you ever feel unsafe at home?

Your in-laws expect your whole salary, your husband calls it tradition, and you're unsure how you could even raise it. That's a difficult position, because it touches your money, your work and your place in the family all at once. It makes sense that you feel stuck about how to begin. How do you feel each month when your salary goes to them?

Looking after your dadi with dementia while keeping up with your studies, and with nobody else helping, is a heavy load. Your love for her comes through clearly, and loving someone doesn't make caring for them alone any less exhausting. It makes sense that it feels like so much. What is the hardest part of caring for her day to day?

A year engaged and the demands for jahez keep growing, and now your father is taking a loan to meet them. Feeling sick about it makes a lot of sense; it's hard to watch someone you love take on debt for your wedding. The joy of the engagement can get buried under all of that. What part of this is weighing on you most right now?

The kid falls sick, it's your fault; guests are unhappy, it's your fault. Being blamed for everything as the daughter-in-law is exhausting and unfair, and it can make you feel you can never get anything right in that house. That frustration comes through clearly in what you wrote. How does it feel when the blame lands on you again?

After the divorce you moved back with your parents and your son, and while they're kind, you feel like a burden on their budget, and relatives look at you as if you failed. That's a lot of weight to carry while you're already rebuilding. Feeling like a burden in your own parents' home can be lonely. What makes you feel that way most?

Not wanting to go to your khala's for Eid makes sense when there's drama every single time. Eid is meant to be a happy day, and dreading it ahead of time takes something away from it. You're allowed to feel this way. What usually happens there that leaves you feeling like this?

You got first position, and instead of anything nice your dad asked why you didn't get an A+ in every subject. That must have hurt, especially when you say he never says anything nice, not even once. Working that hard and still feeling it isn't enough for him is painful. What did you hope he would say when you told him?

Your parents want you to marry your cousin, someone you've known since childhood like a sister. Feeling unable to even say no in your family puts you in a really tight spot, caught between what they expect and what feels right to you. That kind of pressure can feel isolating. What do you think would happen if you told them how you feel?

Dreading tonight makes sense: your taya bringing up how you left engineering for teaching, everyone laughing as if it's a joke, and Abbu saying nothing. Being laughed at for a choice you made is hard, and your father's silence seems to hurt in its own way. It's a lot to walk into at a family dinner. What is it like for you when Abbu stays quiet?

With your fiance in Riyadh, the time difference and his shifts mean you barely get to talk, and you're feeling the two of you drift. Distance can make even a strong bond feel uncertain, especially when the small daily conversations disappear. It makes sense that this worries you. What do you miss most from the times you could talk more?

Always giving more than you get in friendships, and then feeling stupid and used, sounds really hurtful. Being generous with people is a good quality, and it hurts when it isn't returned. It's hard to keep showing up when you feel taken for granted. When did you last feel this way with a friend?

Six months into an arranged marriage, he's decent but you don't feel close to him yet, and you're wondering whether something is wrong with you. That's an honest question, and it takes some courage to ask it. Closeness can grow at its own pace, and it's fine to want more of it. What do you imagine feeling close to him would look like?

Fighting with your wife every day now, over dishes, the TV and the kids' homework, when you two used to laugh a lot, sounds sad and tiring. Missing that easy laughter seems to be part of what hurts most. It's hard when small things keep turning into fights. When do you think things started to change between you?

Your husband gets jealous when you talk to male colleagues, even about work, and it's making office awkward for you. That's a hard spot, because you need to do your job and you're also carrying his reaction into every conversation. It makes sense that it's wearing on you. How does he react when he finds out you've talked with a colleague, and do you feel safe with him?

Ten years of friendship ending over money, and now you don't speak at all, is a real loss. When you say it feels like losing family, that tells me how close you were. Grieving a friendship like this can hurt in ways people don't always recognise. What do you miss most about your friend?

That's a really honest question, and it can be hard to untangle, because loneliness can make anyone who pays attention feel special. At the same time, real liking can show up when we're lonely too. Noticing what draws you to this person might help you see it more clearly. When you think about them, what is it that you find yourself wanting?

He forgot your birthday, and when you were hurt, he said you're making a big deal of it. Now you're doubting your own reaction, even though it clearly hurt. A birthday can feel like a sign of whether you're remembered, so it makes sense it stung. What did you hope would happen on your birthday?

Two years of CSS prep, still in the library while friends have jobs, salaries and cars, and sometimes wondering if you're wasting your life. That comparison can be really heavy, because you're putting in years of effort without anything visible to show for it yet. It's tiring to keep going on faith. What made you choose CSS in the first place?

Being the only woman in your department and getting talked over in every meeting is frustrating and unfair. It makes sense that being repeatedly ignored is starting to make you doubt yourself, even though being talked over says more about the room than about your skills. That can be really isolating. What happens in those meetings when you try to speak?

Feeling like an imposter in your masters, surrounded by people who went to better schools, can be really unsettling. It's easy to start thinking you don't belong, even though you earned your place in the program. That doubt can sit with you in every class. When does the feeling hit hardest?

Five times now your supervisor has rejected your thesis draft without telling you what's wrong. That's frustrating, and it makes sense your confidence is taking a hit when you're working without any direction. It's hard to improve when no one shows you where. How are you feeling about going back to it now?

Twenty-five thousand a month, forty kids in every class, and while you love the kids, you hate feeling so undervalued. Both of those are real, and caring about your students doesn't make the low pay or the workload hurt any less. It can be draining to give so much and get so little back. What makes you feel most undervalued at the school?

An offer abroad that means leaving your parents alone is a really hard choice, with your career pulling one way and family the other. There's no easy answer when both matter so much to you. It makes sense that you can't decide. When you picture saying yes, and then picture saying no, what feelings come up in each?

Being behind in maths with papers coming up is stressful, especially when the academy teacher goes too fast and you're too shy to ask in front of everyone. That leaves you stuck, because the help is right there but asking feels too exposing. Plenty of students feel the same in a big class. Which part of the maths feels most confusing right now?

Your best friend died in a road accident on the motorway just last month, and you still have his voice notes. You can't bring yourself to delete them, and you can't bear to listen to them either. That in-between place makes so much sense when the loss is this fresh. What is it like for you to see them there on your phone?

Your uncle raised you, and he died while you were abroad, and you couldn't get a flight in time for the janaza. It's so painful to miss saying goodbye to someone who was like a parent to you. The thought that you failed him seems to come from how much he meant to you. What do you most wish you could have told him?

Losing your job, your engagement breaking and your nana dying, all in one year, is a lot of loss to hold at once. It makes sense the sadness has blurred together so you can't tell which one it's about anymore. That much grief in a short time would weigh on anyone. When the sadness comes up, what does it feel like?

Four months since your wife died, and now your little ones are asking when she's coming back, while you're grieving her yourself. That question must be so painful to hear. Many parents find that simple, honest words work best at that age, like saying her body stopped working and she can't come back, and pairing that with a lot of reassurance and hugs. Some also lean on family or a child psychologist for support. What has your 5-year-old been asking most?

Fine for a week, and then something as small as a song playing in a rickshaw and you're crying again. Grief coming in waves like that can catch you off guard, especially when you thought you were steadier. Those small moments seem to carry the person straight back to you. Who is it you've been missing when the waves come?

Everyone pretending things are normal, nobody making her sheer khurma, and you going to her room and just sitting there for an hour. That missing dish says so much about how big the gap is today. Sitting in her room sounds like a way of being close to her when everyone else is carrying on. What was it like for you, sitting there?

Sleeping at fajr and waking at asr since the break can leave the whole day feeling upside down, and it makes sense you want it back. People usually go one of two ways: shifting bedtime earlier by a little each night, or picking a fixed wake-up time and getting morning light even after a short night. Some also find a calm wind-down without the phone helps. Which of those sounds more doable for you right now?

Sleeping a full eight hours and still waking as if you hadn't slept at all is really draining, and confusing too, because you're doing the part that's supposed to work. Waking unrefreshed day after day can wear down your mood and energy. If it has been going on for a few weeks, it's worth having a doctor take a look. How long has it been like this?

Your body is tired but your brain keeps running, and even though tomorrow is a normal day, you're already dreading how exhausted you'll be. That worry about not sleeping can become its own thing that keeps you awake. If you'd like, we could try a slow paced breathing exercise here together to help the body settle. Would you like to try that, or would you rather talk for a bit?

With your kids settled in the UK and Canada and their father gone, the house has become so quiet that you leave the TV on just for the sound. That quiet can feel very heavy in a home that was once full. Wanting some voice in the room makes a lot of sense. What are your days usually like now?

Living in a joint family of twelve people and still feeling that no one really knows you sounds very lonely. Being surrounded by people while feeling invisible can hurt even more than being alone, because the closeness is right there but out of reach. It makes sense that you feel this way. What do you wish the people at home understood about you?

After A levels, your school friends scattered to different cities and different lives, while you're still here doing the same things. That can feel lonely, as if everyone moved forward and left you standing in the same spot. Missing them and the life you shared is a real loss. What do you miss most about those days?

Wanting to marry someone your parents don't accept puts you in a really painful spot, between people you love on both sides. People in this situation usually try a few different paths: giving the family time to get to know the person, asking an elder they trust to speak for them, or having one more honest conversation about what their parents fear. None of these is easy. What do you think worries your parents most about this person?

Moving to a new city at thirty and finding everyone already has their circles can feel lonely and a bit discouraging. Some people find it easier to meet others through something regular, like a class, a sports group or volunteering, where seeing the same faces each week slowly turns into friendship. Others start by saying yes to one invitation from work. What kind of people do you find yourself missing having around?

Two hours of commuting every day on top of studies is a lot, and it makes sense that you're tired. Some students use part of the commute to rest rather than study, others try to keep a steadier sleep time even on weekends, and some fit in a short break between classes to recharge. I'd like to hear more about your day before suggesting more. What does your usual day look like from waking up to going to bed?

Overthinking every message you send can be exhausting, and it sounds like you want something practical. Some people find it helps to give themselves a short time limit before hitting send, while others notice the worried thought and gently ask how likely it really is. Some also wait a few minutes after sending before checking for a reply. Which of these feels closest to something you'd try?

Getting nervous and going blank in an interview can be so frustrating, especially when you know your stuff. Some people find it helps to practise answers out loud beforehand, so the words feel familiar, while others find a slow breath in the moment gives them time to recover. It's also fine to say 'let me think about that for a moment'. What tends to happen just before you blank out?

Wanting to tell your parents about a gap year while expecting them to see it as wasting time is a hard conversation to walk into. Some people share a clear plan for the year so parents can see what it's for, while others start by asking what worries their parents most and answer that. It can also help to choose a calm time to talk. What would you most want them to understand about why you want this year?

Forty-eight degrees in Multan with no light is brutal; that kind of heat makes everything feel heavier, from sleeping to thinking straight. It's hard to rest or get anything done when there's no fan to fall back on. I hope you've managed to find some shade and water. How are you getting through the hottest part of the day?

Kalma Chowk traffic every single day sounds like a real test of patience. Sitting in that jam with horns all around you can drain your energy before the day has even started, and doing it daily makes it worse. It's no wonder it feels like the traffic has it in for you. How long does it usually take you to get through it?

A generator roaring right next door is enough to drive anyone up the wall, especially when you're trying to sleep. People cope in different ways, like earplugs, a fan or white noise to cover the sound, or sleeping in the room farthest from it. Some also have a polite word with the neighbour about timing. What's been working for you so far, if anything?

Seventeen revisions of the same logo would test anyone's patience. Changing the same small details again and again, with the client still not happy, can feel endless and a bit pointless. It makes sense you're fed up at this point. What kind of changes are they asking for this time?

Your groupmates haven't done their slides, the presentation is tomorrow, and once again you're the one picking up the slack. It's really frustrating to feel like you always end up carrying the group, and that 'whatever' sounds tired as much as annoyed. Doing it all yourself, again, the night before is a lot. How much is left to get done before tomorrow?

Light gone since six, the UPS dead by ten, your phone on four percent, and you're still trying to finish a client file on mobile data. That's a lot of frustration piling up, and 'this country man' says it all. Working against everything just to get one file out is exhausting. How close are you to finishing it?

The tanker guy charging double because of the shortage in your block, and you had no choice but to pay. Being squeezed when you need something as basic as water is infuriating, and it makes sense you're fuming. It can feel like there's no way to push back. What's bothering you most about it?

The school van uncle quitting without notice has turned your mornings upside down: dropping the kids at 7:15 and still reaching Gulberg by eight just isn't possible. That kind of sudden change is stressful, especially when both the kids and work depend on you being on time. It makes sense that it feels impossible. How did this morning go?

Fuel prices up again, and now you're calculating every trip and asking whether the market can wait two more days. Having to weigh every small outing like that is tiring, and it can make life feel tighter and smaller. It's a constant background worry. How has it been changing your week?

In the NADRA queue from six in the morning, more than two hundred people ahead of you, a day off taken just for this, and it's still not done. That's so frustrating, especially when you gave up the whole day to it. Waiting that long and leaving without it finished can feel like the day was simply taken from you. What do you have to do now to get it sorted?

A 'quick task' at 6:45 on a Friday evening that turned out to be anything but quick. That's frustrating, especially right when you were ready to switch off for the weekend. It can feel like your own time doesn't count. How long did it end up keeping you?

Eighty-five thousand handed over as an advance, and now the solar guy doesn't pick up. That's a painful amount to possibly lose, and it makes sense you're angry. People stopping calling can feel like a second loss, as if everyone has moved on and left you holding it. What are the quiet days like for you now?

Weeks of talking only about bills and the kids' homework can leave you feeling more like co-managers of a household than two people who chose each other. It makes sense that you'd miss a proper chat, the kind that's just about the two of you. Life with kids and bills can crowd that out without anyone meaning it to. What did your proper chats used to be about?

Wondering if anyone would notice if you stopped reaching out is a painful question to sit with, and I can hear the hurt underneath it. Always being the one to text first can start to feel like you care more than they do. Some people hold back out of habit or shyness rather than not caring, though that doesn't make it hurt less. What made this come up for you now?

Working ten-hour days and then hearing that you don't help with the kids can feel unfair, and yet part of you is wondering if she has a point. That openness says you care about getting this right, not just about winning the argument. Both things can be true: you're tired, and she might be stretched too. What does a usual evening look like once you get home?

Lending fifty thousand for your friend's wedding and then watching a whole year go by without a word about it is a heavy thing to carry quietly. It makes sense that it feels awkward, because bringing it up risks the friendship and keeping quiet keeps the resentment going. Plenty of people get stuck right there. What worries you most about bringing it up with her?

Feeling left out in your own home, while your wife spends evening after evening on the phone with her sister, is a lonely place to be. It may not be about the calls themselves so much as the evenings no longer feeling like they belong to the two of you. Wanting more of that time with her is a very human thing. What would you want those evenings to look like?

Three months into marriage and still feeling shy around him, and when everyone just says it's normal, that 'but' at the end tells me it doesn't quite settle the feeling for you. Being told something is normal doesn't make it feel any less awkward when you're the one living it. I'd like to hear what's behind the 'but'. What do you wish people understood about how it feels?

Even if it was accidental, seeing the group trip photo with you cropped out still stings, and both of those can be true at once. It's hard when you want to give your friend the benefit of the doubt and still can't shake the feeling of being left out. A moment like that can make you wonder where you stand in the group. What went through your mind when you saw it?

Saying something sharp this morning and then facing silence from your husband all day is uncomfortable, and I can hear that you want to fix it. It's honest of you to name your ego as the thing in the way. Sometimes a small message owning the sharp words, without a full apology speech, is easier than the big conversation. What's the hardest part about reaching out to him?

Fifteen years of history with someone and suddenly nothing to talk about is a strange, quiet kind of sadness. People do outgrow friendships, and it doesn't erase what the two of you shared. Sometimes a friendship changes shape rather than ending, becoming more occasional, and other times it gently fades. What do you feel when you imagine letting it drift?

Having the same argument about Lahore or Karachi again and again can be draining, especially when it's tied to where your whole married life will start. Usually a repeat argument is about more than the cities themselves, things like family, work, or where each of you feels at home. Different things probably pull at each of you when you picture life in either place. What makes the city you'd choose feel so important to you?

So you believe him about the shop keeping him busy, and still your mind keeps filling the silence with stories. That's something a worried mind does a lot, especially going from talking every day to two days of nothing. If you like, we could gently look at one of those stories together and see how much of it is backed by what he's actually told you. What kind of stories does your mind keep making up?

Being pushed toward a second child when your first is only six months old, and not feeling ready, is a lot to be carrying. It's even harder when your husband stays quiet and you're left facing his mother's expectations on your own. Not being ready is a real feeling, and it deserves to be heard. What happens when you try to talk to your husband about it?

Same parents, same house, and yet your brother can stay out till eleven while you have to be home by maghrib, no wonder it feels unfair. Being treated differently by your own parents can hurt more than the curfew itself. It can start to feel like the rules say something about how much you're trusted. What reason do your parents give when you bring it up?

Being the eldest son and expected to pay for your sisters' weddings is a huge weight at 27, especially when you genuinely want to help. You're caught between love for your sisters and the reality of what one person your age can carry. Both of those deserve space. What part of it feels heaviest right now, the money, the expectation, or something else?

Your ammi reading your diary at 19 sounds like it hurt, because that was the one place meant to be just yours. Feeling like you have no privacy anywhere in the house can be suffocating, especially at an age when you're becoming your own person. It makes sense that this has shaken how safe your space feels. What happened when you found out she'd read it?

A nice boy on video call, a move all the way to Norway, and everyone around you already saying yes, that's a lot of momentum when you haven't decided yet. It can feel like your own feelings are being rushed past in all the excitement. Your answer matters here more than anyone else's. Where are you, honestly, with the idea of moving that far?

Having your husband agree with you in private and then side with his mother in front of everyone sounds confusing and hurtful. It can leave you feeling alone in the moments that matter most, as if his support only exists behind closed doors. I can see why that gap would sting. What happens inside you when he does that in front of the family?

Hearing chachi tell everyone you're too dark for a good rishta is hurtful, and having your mother laugh it off can make it sting even more. It may feel like no one is standing up for you, even in your own family. Comments about skin colour cut deep, and it makes sense that this one stayed with you. How did it feel when your mother laughed it off?

Being caught between your son and your husband, after your son married someone of his own choice, puts you in a really painful spot. You may be trying to keep peace at home while also not wanting to lose your son or push his wife away. That's a lot to hold on your own. What does being in the middle look like for you day to day?

You're caught between two people you love: your ammi, alone in Sahiwal since Abbu passed last year, and your wife, who isn't ready for her to move in. Wanting to look after your mother while also respecting your wife's feelings is a real bind, and there's grief for your father sitting underneath all of it. It makes sense if you feel pulled in both directions. What do you understand about why your wife isn't ready yet?

At 17, having both your parents bring their money fights to you, each complaining about the other, is a heavy thing to carry. It puts you in a grown-up's role in the middle of their problems, when you're still their child. Many people in your place end up feeling responsible for keeping the peace. How does it feel when one of them starts complaining to you?

Studying fine arts at NCA while your cousins are all in medicine or engineering, and then sitting through family gatherings just eating quietly, sounds like a lonely way to spend those evenings. It can feel like there's no easy place for your path in those conversations. Choosing something you care about takes its own kind of courage. What happens at those gatherings that makes you go quiet?

So your father-in-law wants your husband to leave his job for the family hardware business, and neither of you wants that. At least you two are on the same side, even if saying no to his father may still feel hard. Turning down a parent's plan for a family business can carry a lot of weight. How is your husband feeling about telling his father?

Mithai already ordered, the pink suit picked out for you, and you haven't even properly seen the guy's picture. With everyone around you excited, it can feel like the day is moving ahead without you, and your own hesitation has nowhere to go. Not feeling excited makes sense when you know so little about him. What would help you feel a bit more part of this, rather than carried along by it?

So you go to your room and put headphones on to get away from the criticism, and then you get called rude for not sitting with the guests. That's a frustrating trap, where the one way you've found to cope gets you in trouble too. Watching your ammi just smile through it probably makes it harder to say anything yourself. What would make sitting with the guests a bit more bearable for you?

Abbu saying it depends on the in-laws and Ammi asking why you'd want to when you don't have to, no wonder you came away feeling like a child asking for permission. Saying it out loud took something, and their answers seemed to brush past what working means to you. That can sting more than a clear no. What does working after marriage mean to you?

You're genuinely happy for your brother, and at the same time you've quietly become the one paying the household bills while your parents' savings go to the wedding. Nobody asking whether that's okay with you is what seems to hurt. Being relied on without being asked can make you feel invisible, even in a family you love. What would you want them to say to you, if they did ask?

Having your team lead rewrite your whole proposal and then present it as a 'team effort' would sting, especially when being junior made speaking up feel impossible in that moment. Staying quiet doesn't mean you didn't mind; often it just means the stakes felt too high. It's hard to watch your work change hands like that. What bothers you most about it now, the rewrite or the credit?

Getting asked for revision after revision without extra pay, while worrying that one review could hurt your profile, puts you in a really tight spot on Upwork. The fear of saying no makes sense when reviews feel like your livelihood. If you'd like, we could think about how a reply might sound that holds the line without feeling like a refusal. What feels scariest about pushing back with these clients?

Nodding along in meetings and then quietly googling acronyms in the washroom is such a relatable first-job moment, and it also sounds tiring to keep up. Feeling like everyone else speaks a language you haven't learned yet can make you worry you're behind. Most of those acronyms are just workplace habits, not a test you're failing. How do you feel about asking someone on your team what they mean?

Getting WhatsApp calls from your boss on Sundays, when you're on salary and not on call, eats into the one day that should be yours. It makes sense to feel irritated, and maybe stuck, because ignoring a boss doesn't feel like a simple option. Even expecting a call can make it hard to switch off for the whole day. What do you usually do when the call comes on a Sunday?

Going back for a masters at 38 and walking into a class full of 22-year-olds who look at you like the teacher, I can see the funny side, and probably a bit of awkwardness too. Being the one who stands out in a room can make it harder to just be another student. You chose this for a reason, and that counts for something. How are you finding being in class with them so far?

Being the one who explains everything at 9pm on Discord sounds tiring, especially when you came hoping to learn something too. Helping others can be satisfying, but not when it leaves your own studying stuck in place. It's easy to slide into a role in a group that's hard to step out of. What were you hoping to get out of the group when you joined?

Two papers before you defend, with one still half-written, is a big gap between where you are and where your supervisor wants you to be. That can feel overwhelming, especially if the defence date already feels close. It makes sense if the second paper feels like a mountain when the first isn't finished yet. How are you feeling about it right now, more stuck or more pressured?

Staying till eight to finish work you share while your colleague leaves at five, and then hearing your manager praise you both the same, would leave anyone feeling unseen. Your extra three hours a day seem to vanish into one shared 'well done'. That kind of unfairness builds up quietly over time. How long has it been going on like this?

Driving test tomorrow at nine, and your stomach has been flipping since lunch, it's like your body is already living in tomorrow morning. Nerves the day before a test are tiring because there's nothing to actually do with them yet. If it would help, I can guide you through some slow, paced breathing right here in the chat to settle things a little. What's going through your mind when you picture the test?

Your heart jumping every time your phone buzzes with an email from your supervisor sounds exhausting, like being on alert all day waiting for the next one. That kind of reaction often builds up when something about those emails has started to feel threatening. If the racing has been going on for weeks, it's worth having a doctor check it too, so you're not left wondering. What do you usually expect those emails to say?

Getting that jittery 'something will go wrong' feeling before every family function, and then nothing does, can be confusing and tiring. It's as if your mind is bracing for a storm that keeps not arriving. If you like, we could gently look at that thought and what it's actually expecting. What do you imagine might go wrong, when that feeling starts?

Cold, sweaty hands every time you have to speak in the staff meeting, and then on top of it the voice saying you're 46 and should be over this. That second part can be harder than the nerves themselves, because it turns a feeling into a failing. Nerves like these don't run on a timetable, and there's no age at which they're supposed to stop. What goes through your mind just before it's your turn to speak?

Twenty minutes late from tuition, and your mind has already raced ahead to the worst, that's a horrible feeling to sit with while you wait. Worry tends to fill silence with the scariest stories it can find. If it helps while you're waiting, we could do a quick 5-4-3-2-1 grounding together to bring you back to the room for a moment. What usually holds him up on days when he's late?

A tight throat every time you have to call your in-laws, even though they're not mean, sounds confusing and uncomfortable. Sometimes our bodies react to the pressure of a situation, like wanting to say the right thing or be seen well, more than to the people themselves. If the tightness shows up at other times too, it's worth getting it checked by a doctor. What does a phone call with them usually feel like for you?

A background hum of worry all day, with nothing obvious to point to, can be really wearing, partly because there's nothing to fix or argue with. I can't tell you what it is, but if it's been with you for weeks, it's worth talking to a psychologist or doctor, who can look at it properly. Sometimes the hum gets louder at certain times or in certain places. When do you notice it most during the day?

Feeling restless every evening around maghrib, as though something bad is about to happen, is unsettling, especially when you can't point to a reason. Evenings can carry a particular weight for some people, with the light changing and the day closing. If it's been happening for weeks, a psychologist could help you make sense of it. What's usually going on around you at that time of the evening?

Your heart racing, not getting a full breath, hands tingling, all while driving, must have been really frightening, and you did well to pull over on the service lane. It makes sense that you're scared to get back in the car tomorrow. Since it was such a strong physical experience, it would be good to have a doctor check you over, so you're not left guessing what happened. What feels scariest about driving tomorrow?

The fear is that this client complains to your boss and, four months in, you end up looking careless. You caught the mistake yourself and sent a correction, which is what a careful person does, even though your body is still buzzing and the inbox keeps pulling you back. If you'd like, a few minutes of paced breathing here might take the edge off the buzzing. What do you think your boss would actually say if they did hear about it?

Heavy, and without a clear reason, can be one of the more confusing ways to feel, because there's nothing obvious to point at. Sometimes the heaviness shows up first and the reasons, if there are any, come later, or not at all. You don't have to explain it to be allowed to feel it. Where do you notice the heaviness most, in your body or in your thoughts?

Posting funny memes while feeling kind of empty inside means the version of you your friends see isn't the whole picture. Not unhappy, just empty, is a hard feeling to explain, and it can feel even lonelier when everyone assumes you're fine. Empty can be harder to put into words than sad, because there's no clear thing to point at. What does the empty feeling look like in your days?

Retired, with the kids grown and busy with their own lives, and the days slipping past so quietly you can't say what you did with any of them. That kind of blur can feel strange after years when every day had a shape and people who needed you. It's a big change, even when it's an expected one. What does an ordinary day look like for you now?

Not resting, just there, the whole weekend on your bed, that sounds like a heavy, flat kind of stuck rather than a choice to relax. It can be unsettling when time off arrives and you can't do anything with it. If weekends have felt like this for a few weeks, it's worth talking to a psychologist or doctor about it. How have you been feeling during the week, outside the weekend?

Lying on the sofa since asr, scrolling through things you can't even remember, and feeling not sad, just nothing. That kind of blank can be strange to sit in, because there's nothing obvious to name or fix. Sometimes scrolling fills the space so we don't have to notice how flat things feel. How long have your days been feeling like this?

Nothing happened, and yet after smiling at everyone all day you came home feeling dull, and the lack of a reason seems to make it stranger. Sometimes the effort of keeping up a bright face at work is enough on its own to leave you flat by evening. Dull days without a cause are still worth paying attention to. How often has this dull feeling been showing up lately?

Missing being someone's first call is such a specific, tender kind of loneliness, and you're kind enough not to blame anyone for being busy. It's not that people are gone, it's that you don't feel like the one someone reaches for first anymore. That can quietly ache, even when life is otherwise okay. Who used to call you first, and what did that feel like?

Two years of working from home, and some days the only conversation you have is with the delivery rider, that's a lot of quiet to live inside. Working from home can slowly shrink the small daily contact we don't notice until it's gone. It's easy for days like that to start feeling heavy. How are you feeling about how quiet your days have become?

When every conversation with your friends turns to schools and nappies, it's easy to feel like you've been left outside a club you didn't join. That sense of not fitting anymore can be lonely, especially with people who used to feel like home. It doesn't mean the friendships are gone, but something has shifted. What do you miss most about how things were with them?

Saturday night, lying in bed watching other people's stories go by, can bring a particular kind of lonely, as if everyone else's night is happening somewhere you're not. It's not the phone itself so much as what it shows you while you're on your own. I'm glad you said it out loud here. How are you feeling as you watch them?

Eid being okay, but spending most of it on your phone while everyone else laughed together, sounds lonely in a way that's hard to explain to the people around you. Sometimes the phone becomes a place to be when it's hard to find a way into the room. It can feel like being there and not there at the same time. What made it hard to join in?

After your divorce, losing your couple friends to his side means you lost a whole circle along with the marriage, and that's a lot of loss at once. No wonder talking here has felt easier than reaching out to people. I'm glad these chats help, and you also deserve people of your own, friends who are there for you and not for the two of you as a pair. Who in your life, even from before the marriage, has felt like yours?

Napping after maghrib and then lying wide awake till three is a frustrating loop, and I can hear you blaming yourself for it. The nap probably feels impossible to resist because by that time you're genuinely tired, which isn't a failing. Looking at what that evening time is like for you might show what makes the nap so hard to skip. What's going on in your day just before the nap pulls you in?

The papers are over, and yet your body is still waking you at five in a panic, as if there's one more exam to write. After weeks of pressure the body can hold on to that rhythm, and if it keeps happening for a few more weeks, a doctor or psychologist could help. Waking like that every morning sounds exhausting. When you wake with that panic, what helps, even a little, to settle it?

Do maheene se kaam ka paisa atka hua hai aur ab apna kharcha chalana bhi ek sawal ban gaya hai, yeh bohat bechaini wali jagah hai. Mehnat kar ke bhi haath khaali rehna ghussa bhi dilata hai aur fikar bhi. Upar se client ke peeche bhaagna alag thakan hai. Is waqt sab se zyada dabao kis cheez ka hai, client se paise nikalwane ka ya is mahine ke kharche poore karne ka?

Committee ki qist sar par hai, paise poore nahi, aur kisi se maangne ka soch kar hi sharam aa jati hai. Yeh do taraf ka dabao hai, ek taraf waqt par qist dene ki fikar aur saath hi apni izzat ka khayal. Aisi sharam aksar un logon ko hoti hai jo hamesha khud sambhalne ki koshish karte hain. Kisi se maangne ka sochte hi dil mein sab se zyada kya khayal aata hai?

Garmi, bijli nahi, UPS bhi jawab de gaya aur bachay ro rahe hain, aise mein dimagh bhi saath chhorne lagta hai. Bachon ko takleef mein dekhna apni garmi se zyada bhaari lagta hai. Kuch log aise waqt bachon ka munh haath thande paani se dhulwa dete hain ya un par geela kapra rakh dete hain, kuch ghar ka sab se thanda kona dhoondh lete hain, aur kuch thori der ke liye kisi rishtedar ya padosi ke ghar chale jate hain jahan bijli ho. In mein se is waqt kya mumkin lag raha hai?

Aaj kal chhoti chhoti baaton par ghussa aa raha hai, aur andar se lag raha hai ke shayad yeh stress ki wajah se hai. Aksar jab andar bohat kuch jama ho jata hai to choti si baat bhi aakhri qatra ban jati hai. Ghussa aane ke baad aksar khud se bhi naraazgi hoti hai. In dinon zindagi mein aisa kya chal raha hai jo zehan par sab se zyada bhaari para hua hai?

Pasine mein baith kar hisaab lagana aur phir yeh dekhna ke mahine ke 12 din baqi hain aur paise sirf 3 din ke, yeh garmi se bhi zyada bhaari ehsaas hoga. Bijli ke baghair lamba din aur upar se paison ki yeh fikar, dono mil kar bohat thaka dete hain. Is waqt sab se zyada kis cheez ki fikar khaye ja rahi hai, ghar ka khana, bills, ya kuch aur?

Metro bus mein achanak dil itni zor se dharakna ke lage gir jaunga, yeh bohat darr wala lamha raha hoga, aur ab us ki wajah se bahar nikalna bhi mushkil lag raha hai. Aksar aisa ek tajurba dimagh mein reh jata hai aur phir har bahar ka qadam usi ki yaad dilata hai. Kyun ke yeh jism mein hua, ek dafa doctor se check karwa lena bhi tasalli de sakta hai. Jab ab bahar jaane ka sochte hain to andar kya hota hai?

Do din se bhai ka phone na uthana, aur woh bhi itni door, aise mein dimagh khud hi bure bure khayal banane lagta hai. Jab tak koi khabar na mile, yeh intezaar bohat bechain karta hai. Fikar apni jagah sachi hai, lekin abhi tak kuch pata nahi, aur phone na uthane ki aam wajahen bhi ho sakti hain, jaise kaam ki shift ya phone ka koi masla. Wahan bhai ke aas paas kaun log hain jin se khabar mil sakti hai?

Har saal sardiyon ke aate hi ek udaasi si cha jana, aur pehle se pata hona ke yeh phir aayegi, apne aap mein bhaari baat hai. Jo udaasi baar baar laut kar aaye, us ka bojh aur bhi thaka deta hai. Agar yeh hafton tak rehti hai to kisi psychologist ya doctor se baat karna bhi ek raasta ho sakta hai. Jab yeh udaasi chhati hai to aap ke din kaise badal jate hain?

Khud ko slow mehsoos karna aur sochna bhi mushkil lagna, yeh andar se bohat thaka dene wali kaifiyat hai. Aisa lagta hai jaise dimagh par koi bhaari parda para ho aur har kaam mein do guna zor lag raha ho. Agar yeh kuch hafton se hai to kisi doctor ya psychologist se ek baar baat karna faida de sakta hai. Yeh kaifiyat kab se chal rahi hai, aur din ke kis hisse mein sab se zyada mehsoos hoti hai?

Bas guzar raha hai, aur kaafi dinon se sab pheeka pheeka lagna, kisi cheez mein dil na lagna, yeh ek khamosh si thakan hai jo bahar se nazar nahi aati. Jo cheezein pehle achi lagti theen, un mein bhi rang na rehna andar se khaali kar deta hai. Agar yeh kuch hafton se chal raha hai to kisi psychologist se baat karna bhi ek raasta ho sakta hai. Yeh pheekapan kab se mehsoos ho raha hai?

Na acha na bura, bas kuch nahi, aur yeh kuch nahi wali kaifiyat itne arse se chal rahi hai, yeh apne aap mein thaka deti hai. Kabhi kabhi udaasi se zyada mushkil yahi khaalipan hota hai, kyun ke us ka koi naam bhi samajh nahi aata. Agar yeh hafton se hai to kisi psychologist se is par baat karna madad kar sakta hai. Yeh flat sa ehsaas din ke kis hisse mein sab se zyada mehsoos hota hai?

Rishte wale rang dekh kar mana kar gaye, aur ab ulta ghar walon ke taane bhi sunne par rahe hain, yeh dohri chot hai. Jis cheez par kisi ka koi ikhtiyar hi nahi, us par itna kuch sunna dil ko bohat dukh deta hai. Jahan se sahara ki ummeed ho, wahan se baatein milna aur bhi akela kar deta hai. Ghar walon ki baaton mein sab se zyada kya chubh raha hai?

Bachpan se khala ke bete ke saath rishta tay hai, aur dil mein us ke liye koi lagao hi nahi, yeh bohat uljhan wali jagah hai. Ek taraf khandan ki barson purani baat hai aur us ke saamne apne dil ki sachai. Jo faisla bachpan mein doosron ne kar diya ho, us par apni marzi kehna aksar bohat mushkil lagta hai. Is rishte ke baare mein sochte hue sab se zyada kya mehsoos hota hai?

Solah saal ka beta baat hi na kare aur kamre mein band rahe, to dil fikar bhi karta hai aur samajh bhi nahi aata ke darwaza kaise khulwaya jaye. Is umar mein bachay aksar thora door ho jate hain, lekin yeh doori phir bhi dil ko lagti hai. Kuch log seedhi baat ke bajaye saath koi kaam karte hue ya gaari mein ghoomte hue halki phulki baat se shuru karte hain. Kuch arsa pehle tak beta kin cheezon par khul kar baat karta tha?

Aap dono ki baat ab sirf bachon tak reh gayi hai, aur yeh ehsaas ke beech mein kuch bacha hi nahi, andar se kaafi khaali kar deta hai. Bachon ki zimmedari mein aksar miyan biwi ek doosre ke liye waqt hi nahi nikal paate, aur rishta chupke se sirf ghar chalane ka intezam ban jata hai. Jab aap dono ka rishta sab se acha tha, us waqt kya alag tha?

MDCAT ki tayyari phir se, aur saath mein yeh darr ke agar is baar bhi na hua to ghar walon ka saamna kaise hoga, yeh bohat bhaari bojh hai. Mehnat ke saath saath sharam ka yeh khayal dimagh mein chalta rahe to parhai bhi mushkil ho jati hai. Second attempt ka dabao waise bhi alag hota hai. Ghar walon ke reaction ke baare mein sochte hue sab se zyada kis baat ka darr lagta hai?

Do hafte se supervisor ka jawab nahi aa raha aur submission sar par hai, aise mein intezaar karna bhi mushkil hai aur aage barhna bhi. Jab sab kuch kisi aur ke jawab par atka ho to bebasi aur ghussa dono aate hain. Upar se waqt haath se nikalta mehsoos hota hai. Is waqt project ka kaun sa hissa supervisor ki raaye ke baghair ruka hua hai?

Board ke papers mein do mahine reh gaye hain aur maths samajh hi nahi aa rahi, yeh ghabrahat samajh mein aati hai. Jab koi subject baar baar samajh na aaye to aksar lagta hai ke masla apne andar hai, halankay aksar baat sirf samjhane ke tareeqe ki hoti hai. Maths mein kahan aa kar sab se zyada atak jate hain, formulas, sawalon ko samajhna, ya kuch aur?

Mehnat aap ki aur credit manager le jaye, aur meeting mein chup reh jana, yeh andar hi andar bohat chubhta hoga. Aise mein manager par ghussa bhi aata hai aur kabhi kabhi apni chuppi par khud se naraazgi bhi hoti hai. Yeh dono ehsaas ek saath bohat bhaari hote hain. Meeting mein jab yeh hota hai to us lamhe bolne se kya cheez rokti hai?

Saara kaam aap ne kiya aur marks sab ke barabar, yeh na-insafi ka ehsaas bohat ghussa dilata hai. Upar se jinhon ne kuch nahi kiya woh bhi utne hi number le gaye jitne mehnat karne wale ko mile. Aisa ho to agli dafa group mein kaam karne ka dil bhi nahi karta. Is mein sab se zyada kya bura laga, apni mehnat ka nazar na aana ya group walon ka rawaiya?

Kal Abbu ki barsi hai, teen saal ho gaye, aur un ki chappal ab bhi darwaze ke paas rakhi hai. Kuch cheezein jagah se hatana aisa lagta hai jaise un ki ek aur nishani chali jayegi, isliye woh wahin rehti hain. Barsi se pehle ke din aksar yaadon ko aur qareeb le aate hain. Woh chappal dekh kar aaj kal dil mein kya aata hai?

Aaj aap ka kutta chala gaya, aur woh sirf janwar nahi tha, family ka hissa tha. Aise mein jab log kehte hain ke janwar hi tha, to dukh ke saath akelapan bhi barh jata hai, jaise is gham ko jagah hi na mile. Jo pyaar us ke saath tha woh sacha tha, aur us ka gham bhi utna hi sacha hai. Us ke saath ki kaun si baat is waqt sab se zyada yaad aa rahi hai?

Phuppo ki beti ki shaadi mein sab khush the, aur Dadi ki woh baat dil mein thi ke woh is shaadi par nachengi. Un ki kami us khushi ke beech aur bhi zyada mehsoos hui hogi, isi liye washroom mein ja kar rona aa gaya. Khushi ke mauqon par apnon ki kami aksar sab se zyada chubhti hai. Dadi ke baare mein aaj sab se zyada kya yaad aaya?

Bara baje se 2:40 tak pankhe ko ghoorte rehna, aur saath mein yeh hisaab ke subah aath baje office hai, yeh bohat bechaini wali halat hai. Jitna sone ki koshish karo, utna hi neend door bhaagti lagti hai. Agar dil chahe to yahin ek dheemi saans wali exercise bhi ho sakti hai. Is waqt lete lete dimagh mein kya chal raha hai, koi khaas soch ya bas jism thaka hai aur neend nahi aa rahi?

Kabhi kabhi baat sirf is liye karna ke koi to sune, is mein ek gehri thakan aur akelapan dono nazar aate hain. Main yahan sun rahi hoon, lekin main ek AI hoon, aur dil yeh bhi chahta hoga ke koi insaan ho jo saamne baith kar sune. Yeh khwahish bilkul samajh mein aati hai. Aaj kal yeh ehsaas ke koi nahi sunta, sab se zyada kab aata hai?

Bachon ki shaadiyan ho gayin, sab apne apne gharon mein, aur ab ghar ki khamoshi hai aur aap. Saari zindagi jo ghar shor aur zimmedariyon se bhara raha, us ka achanak khaali ho jana dil par bohat asar karta hai. Is mein bachon ke basne ka sukoon bhi hota hai aur ek kami bhi. Din ka kaun sa waqt is khaali ghar mein sab se zyada bhaari lagta hai?

Exam sar par ho aur dimagh focus hi na kare, to parhne baithna bhi ek jung lagta hai. Kuch log chhote chhote tukron mein parhte hain, jaise bees pachees minute aur phir thora sa break, kuch phone ko doosre kamre mein rakh dete hain, aur kuch parhne se pehle do minute saans par dhyan de kar dimagh ko thehrate hain. Har kisi ke liye alag cheez kaam karti hai. In mein se kaun si cheez aazmane ka dil karta hai?

Saas se baat karni ho aur darr ho ke baat larai mein na badal jaye, yeh bohat nazuk jagah hai. Kuch log aisi baat tab karte hain jab mahaul thanda ho aur koi aur saamne na ho, kuch apni baat 'mujhe aisa lagta hai' se shuru karte hain taa ke ilzaam na lage, aur kuch saas ki baat poori sun kar phir apni baat rakhte hain. In mein se kaun sa tareeqa aap ke ghar ke mahaul mein chal sakta hai?

Bohat tension ho to jism aur dimagh dono kase hue lagte hain, aur sukoon ka raasta dhoondna samajh mein aata hai. Kuch log dheemi saans lete hain, jaise chaar tak saans andar aur chhe tak bahar, kuch 5-4-3-2-1 grounding karte hain jis mein aas paas ki cheezon par dhyan diya jata hai, aur kuch muscles ko kas kar dheela chhorte hain. Yeh teeno yahin chat mein bhi ho sakti hain. In mein se kis ko abhi aazmane ka dil hai?

Ghar walon ko yeh samjhana ke abhi shaadi nahi karni, aksar sab se mushkil baat-cheet lagti hai, kyun ke un ki fikar aur apni marzi dono saath chal rahi hoti hain. Kuch log ghar ke kisi aise fard se baat karte hain jo samajh sake, jaise koi bhai behan ya khala, kuch apni wajah saaf alfaaz mein rakhte hain, jaise parhai ya career, aur kuch waqt ki ek had bata dete hain. Abhi shaadi na karne ke peeche sab se bari wajah kya hai?

Ghussa jaldi aa jana aur us par qaboo na rehna apne aap ko bhi pareshan karta hai. Kuch logon ko us lamhe thori der ke liye jagah se hat jana madad deta hai, kuch dheemi saans lete hain jab tak jism thanda na ho, aur kuch baad mein dekhte hain ke ghussa kin baaton par sab se zyada aata hai. Har kisi ke liye alag cheez kaam karti hai. Aam taur par ghussa kis tarah ki baaton par sab se jaldi aata hai?

Dawai ke baghair neend behtar karne ka sochna samajh mein aata hai. Kuch log har raat ek hi waqt par sone aur uthne ki koshish karte hain, kuch sone se thori der pehle phone door rakh dete hain, aur kuch bistar par let kar dheemi saans ya tense-and-release karte hain, jo yahin chat mein bhi ho sakti hai. Agar neend ka masla hafton se hai to doctor se baat karna bhi faida deta hai. Neend mein sab se zyada mushkil kahan aati hai, sona ya beech mein aankh khulna?

Chhe hafte aur physics sab se kamzor, aise mein samajh nahi aata ke shuru kahan se ho. Kuch log sab se kamzor subject ko subah ka taaza waqt dete hain, kuch physics ke woh chapters pakarte hain jin ke marks zyada aate hain, aur kuch past papers se dekhte hain ke kaun se sawal baar baar aate hain. Har tareeqa alag logon ke kaam aata hai. Physics mein sab se zyada mushkil kya lagti hai, numericals ya theory?

Apna kaam kisi aur ke naam se jata dekhna bohat chubhta hai, aur samajh nahi aata ke baat kis se ki jaye. Ek raasta colleague se seedha aur aaram se baat karna hai, jis se kabhi kabhi masla wahin hal ho jata hai. Manager ko batana bhi ek option hai, khaas taur par agar emails ya files mein saboot ho ke kaam aap ka hai. Kuch log saath saath apna kaam seedha manager ko bhejna shuru kar dete hain. In mein se kaun sa tareeqa office ke mahaul mein theek lagta hai?

Ek hi din mein teen shaadiyan, yeh to poori marathon ho gayi. Har jagah tayyar ho kar jana, salaam dua, khana aur raat der tak baithna, thakan to banti hai. Hansi apni jagah, lekin jism ka haal bhi samajh aata hai. Teeno mein se kaun si shaadi sab se yaadgaar rahi, ya bas ab bistar hi sab se pyaara lag raha hai?

Is garmi mein AC bhi kharab ho jaye to sach mein haal bura ho jata hai. Pasina, chirchirapan aur neend bhi na aaye, sab kuch mushkil lagta hai. Kuch log aise mein geela kapra gardan par rakh lete hain ya ghar ka sab se thanda kamra pakar lete hain. AC theek hone tak din kaise guzaarne ka socha hai?

Iftar mein abhi do ghante baqi hain aur bhook apni intehaa par hai, yeh aakhri ghante aksar sab se lambe lagte hain. Roze ka yeh hissa thakan aur bhook dono saath le aata hai. Kuch log is waqt thora sa let jate hain ya iftar ki tayyari mein lag jate hain taa ke waqt guzar jaye. Aaj iftar mein kis cheez ka sab se zyada intezaar hai?

Is assignment ne to sach mein saari energy nichor li lagti hai. Kabhi kabhi ek kaam itna phail jata hai ke khatam hone ka naam hi nahi leta, aur thakan ke saath chirchirapan bhi aa jata hai. Kasam wali baat bilkul samajh aati hai. Is mein sab se zyada mushkil kya lag raha hai, kaam ki lambai, deadline, ya topic hi samajh nahi aa raha?

Kal ka paper hai aur syllabus abhi tak khatam nahi hua, yeh ghabrahat aur dabao bohat samajh mein aata hai. Aap ne lol ke saath likha hai aur ho sakta hai yeh sirf mazaaq mein kaha ho, lekin khudkushi ka lafz aaya hai to main seedha pooch leti hoon, kyun ke mujhe aap ki parwah hai. Kya sach mein kabhi apni jaan lene ke khayal aate hain, ya yeh sirf paper ka stress bol raha hai?

Ek signal par 45 minute, yeh to sabr ka poora imtihaan hai. Horn, dhuan aur aage barhne ka koi naam nahi, aise mein dimagh garam hona bilkul samajh aata hai. Kabhi kabhi aisi rukawat poore din ka mood bigaar deti hai. Is traffic ke chakkar mein aaj kya kya late ho gaya?

Pakistan ka phir haarna, aur woh bhi aankhon ke saamne, har fan ke liye dil todne wala hota hai. Itni ummeedein laga kar baithna aur phir wahi kahani, ghussa bhi aata hai aur hansi bhi. Cricket ke saath yeh dil ka rishta hi aisa hai. Aaj ke match mein sab se zyada kis baat par dil jala?

Gym ke shuru mein hi trainer ne itna chalaya ke jism ne haath khare kar diye, yeh to gym ka asli welcome hai. Kal subah muscles ka dard shayad yaad dilayega ke aaj kitni mehnat hui. Thakan ke saath andar thori si khushi bhi hogi ke shuruaat to ho gayi. Aaj ke din ke baad gym ke baare mein kaisa lag raha hai?

Teen quizzes, do projects aur ek viva, sab ek hi hafte mein, yeh to sach mein bhaari hafta hai. Itna kuch ek saath ho to dimagh samajh hi nahi pata ke kahan se pakre, aur thakan pehle hi chha jati hai. Aise hafte se zinda nikal aane ki khwahish bilkul samajh aati hai. In sab mein se kis cheez ka sab se zyada bojh lag raha hai?

38k ka bill, woh bhi ek mahine ka, dekh kar to sach mein jhatka lagta hai. Ghar ka budget already tight ho to aisa ek bill poora plan hila deta hai, and the stress makes total sense. Upar se yeh samajh nahi aata ke itna aaya kaise. Is bill ke baad sab se zyada kis cheez ki fikar ho rahi hai, monthly kharche, bachat, ya kuch aur?

Load shedding, UPS khatam, laptop 5% pe, aur submission midnight ko, sab kuch ek saath against lag raha hai. Itni mehnat ke baad bijli ki wajah se deadline miss hone ka darr bohat frustrating hai. Kuch log aise mein teacher ko pehle se email kar dete hain, ya kisi qareeb ki jagah chale jate hain jahan bijli ho. Abhi kaam kitna baqi hai, ya bas upload karna reh gaya hai?

Bank ka kaam, bachon ki fees, gaari ki service, sab ek saath, no wonder brain 40 tabs wala feel kar raha hai. Jab sab kuch urgent lagta hai to kisi ek par focus karna bhi mushkil ho jata hai. Kabhi kabhi saare kaam kaghaz par likh dena dimagh ke kuch tabs band kar deta hai. In mein se kaun sa kaam sab se zyada dimagh mein khatak raha hai?

Bus stop pe dhakke, late pohanchna aur upar se boss ki baatein, desk tak aate aate energy already khatam ho jati hai. Din shuru hone se pehle hi itna kuch jhelna, aur woh bhi roz roz, bohat draining hai. Is poore safar mein sab se zyada kya chubhta hai, rush, boss ki baatein, ya yeh ke yeh roz ka scene hai?

Raat ko achanak dil itna tez dharakna, aur yeh lagna ke kuch seriously galat hai, bohat darr wala experience hai. Abhi bhi haath thande hain, to lagta hai jism abhi tak us darr se nikla nahi. Kyun ke yeh jism mein hua, ek dafa doctor se check karwa lena tasalli de sakta hai. Agar dil chahe to yahin ek dheemi saans wali exercise ho sakti hai jo jism ko thora settle karne mein madad deti hai. Is waqt andar kaisa feel ho raha hai?

Har message bhejne ke baad 'kya maine kuch galat keh diya' wala loop, aur phir do ghante wahi sochte rehna, yeh bohat thaka dene wala hai. Aksar aisa tab hota hai jab logon ki bohat parwah ho aur galti ka darr bhi. Kuch logon ke kaam yeh aata hai ke khud se poochein, is soch ke haq mein asal saboot kya hai. Jab yeh loop shuru hota hai to sab se zyada kis baat ka darr hota hai?

Kal Islamabad ki flight, zindagi mein first time akele travel, aur dimagh mein 'what if I get lost' wala khayal, yeh nervousness bilkul samajh aati hai. Naya tajurba excitement aur darr dono saath laata hai. Kabhi kabhi darr ko thora qareeb se dekhna madad karta hai, jaise yeh sochna ke agar raasta bhool bhi gaye to kya kya options honge. Is trip mein sab se zyada kis hisse ki fikar hai, airport, pohanch kar, ya kuch aur?

300 logon wali mehndi aur crowds pasand nahi, to excuses ka sochna samajh aata hai. Saath mein yeh fikar bhi ke na gaye to sab naraz honge, to yeh beech mein phans jane wali feeling hai. Kuch log aise functions mein thori der ke liye jate hain ya koi khamosh kona dhoondh lete hain. Crowd mein sab se zyada mushkil kya lagta hai, shor, log, ya baat cheet ka pressure?

Gym bhi chhoot gaya, reading bhi, aur ab bas phone scroll, aur andar se yeh ehsaas ke I miss who I used to be. Yeh sirf aadaton ka badalna nahi, apne aap se door ho jane ka dukh lagta hai. Agar yeh kaafi hafton se hai aur mood bhi neeche hai to kisi psychologist se baat karna bhi ek option ho sakta hai. Purane wale aap mein aisa kya tha jo sab se zyada miss hota hai?

Khana banane ka dil hi na kare aur zyada tar Maggi kha kar so jayein, to yeh sawal uthna ke kya yeh bura hai, samajh aata hai. Is ka koi right ya wrong answer nahi, kabhi yeh sirf thakan hoti hai aur kabhi andar ki udaasi ka ishara. Agar yeh kaafi waqt se chal raha hai to kisi doctor ya psychologist se baat karna madad kar sakta hai. Khane ke ilawa aaj kal baqi cheezon mein dil kaisa lagta hai?

Kuch hua bhi nahi, phir bhi andar se khaali khaali, aur jab log poochte hain to nothing kehna hi sach lagta hai. Aisa khaalipan aksar sab se confusing hota hai, kyun ke us ki koi wajah nazar nahi aati jise samjhaya ja sake. Agar yeh feeling kuch hafton se hai to kisi psychologist se baat karna faida de sakta hai. Yeh khaalipan din mein kab sab se zyada mehsoos hota hai?

Abbu ke saath cricket matches dekhna kabhi itni pyaari cheez thi, aur kal final tha lekin dekhne ka dil hi nahi kiya. Jo cheez kabhi itni khushi deti thi, us mein dil na lagna andar se kuch kho jane jaisa lagta hai. Yeh chhoti si baat nahi, aur is ka dukh hona samajh aata hai. Final na dekhne par andar kya feel hua?

Har roz cousin se comparison, 1080 aur 960 ka hisaab, aur upar se yeh lagna ke ghar wale samajhte hain koshish hi nahi ki, yeh bohat hurt karta hai. 960 tak pohanchne mein jo mehnat lagi, woh is comparison mein kahin gum ho jati hai. Roz roz yeh sunna andar se thaka deta hai. Jab yeh comparison hota hai to us waqt andar sab se zyada kya feel hota hai?

24 saal ki umar, aur bahen ki shaadi aur Abbu ke loan ki zimmedari dono aap ke kandhon par, yeh bohat bhaari bojh hai. Ghar ke liye karna bhi hai aur andar se yeh awaaz bhi ke meri bhi koi life hai, aur dono feelings ek saath sach ho sakti hain. Beta hone ki yeh zimmedari aksar bina pooche hi mil jati hai. Apni life ke liye is waqt sab se zyada kis cheez ki kami mehsoos ho rahi hai?

Bhai cheezein bina pooche le leta hai, Ammi hamesha us ki side leti hain, aur sorry har baar aap ko hi kehna parta hai. Is mein sirf cheezon ka masla nahi lagta, shayad yeh feeling bhi hai ke ghar mein baat suni hi nahi jati, and that really hurts. Har baar khud jhukna andar ghussa jama kar deta hai. Jab Ammi us ki side leti hain to us waqt dil mein kya aata hai?

Engagement ho gayi aur us waqt haan kehne ke ilawa koi raasta hi nazar nahi aaya, aur ab andar regret hai. Jab faisla dabao mein ho to baad mein woh apna nahi lagta, aur yeh bohat bhaari feeling hai. Regret ke saath confusion bhi hoga ke ab kya ho sakta hai. Yeh regret is waqt sab se zyada kis baat par hai, rishte par, us insaan par, ya yeh ke marzi poochi hi nahi gayi?

Job jaane ka dukh pehle hi kaafi tha, aur ab phuppo ne poore khandan mein baat phaila di, to har call par sympathy sunna aur embarrassing ho jata hai. Jo baat apne waqt aur apne tareeqe se batani thi, woh kisi aur ne bata di, aur yeh control chhin jane wali feeling hai. In calls mein sab se zyada kya chubhta hai, sympathy ya yeh ke baat bina pooche phaili?

Har waqt location maangna, aur sab kehte hain yeh pyaar hai, lekin andar se ghutan mehsoos ho rahi hai, aur yeh feeling apni jagah bilkul sach hai. Jab koi cheez pyaar ke naam par di jaye lekin saans lena mushkil lage, to confusion hona samajh aata hai. Suffocating wala ehsaas aksar kisi baat ki taraf ishara hota hai. Location ke ilawa kya aur cheezon mein bhi aisa control hota hai, jaise kis se milna hai ya phone check karna, aur kya kabhi us ke ghusse se darr bhi lagta hai?

MDCAT ka second attempt, aur saath mein yeh darr ke agar is baar bhi na hua to ghar walon ko kya bataya jayega, yeh bohat bhaari pressure hai. Prep ke saath yeh soch bhi chalti rahe to focus karna aur mushkil ho jata hai. Itni mehnat ke baad bhi yeh khauf rehna thaka deta hai. Ghar walon ke baare mein sochte hue sab se zyada kis cheez ka darr hai, un ki disappointment ya kuch aur?

Raat ko US clients ke saath calls, aur din mein ghar wale samajhte hain ke aap farigh hain, yeh double thakan hai jo kisi ko nazar hi nahi aati. Jab neend aur kaam ka schedule hi ulta ho aur log usay chhutti samjhein, to nobody gets it wali feeling bilkul samajh aati hai. Din mein ghar walon ki taraf se sab se zyada kya expect kiya jata hai?

Do saal ki mehnat ke baad CSS ka result fail aaya, aur upar se yeh ke sab ko itna yaqeen tha, yeh dohra dukh hai. Apni disappointment ke saath logon ki ummeedon ka bojh bhi aa jata hai. Itne arse ki mehnat ka yun result aana kisi nuqsan jaisa lagta hai. Is waqt is result ke saath sab se bhaari kya lag raha hai?

Performance improvement plan aur 60 din ki ginti, aur har qadam par nazar, yeh watched wali feeling bohat uncomfortable hoti hai. Aise mein kaam karna bhi mushkil ho jata hai kyun ke har cheez test jaisi lagti hai. Saath mein job ki fikar bhi dimagh ke peeche chalti rehti hogi. Jab se yeh plan shuru hua hai, din mein sab se zyada stress kis waqt hota hai?

Pichle saal accident mein dost ko khona, aur aaj us ki birthday hai, aur number abhi bhi phone mein saved hai.
